newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Six bidders for Argentine oil firm Bridas.
newsitem.headline: Six bidders for Argentine oil firm Bridas.

text.p: Six international oil firms offered to buy part or all of Argentine oil and gas firm Bridas Energy Corp, an oil sector source said Friday.

The bidders were U.S companies Amoco and Union Texas Petroleum, France's Total, Anglo-Dutch group Shell, Spain's Endesa and a consortium formed by Spain's Repsol and U.S. Mobil, the source told Reuters.
Details of the offers made in New York were not available.
Bridas, controlled by Argentine family Bulgheroni, is looking for a strategic partner to expand its international business.

"Brida's shareholders expect an offer that will allow them to keep control," the source said. "So, the price for 100 percent of the firm woul not be proportional to, say, the price for a 45 percent stake. It would be much higher."
The source said some some of the bidders were considering forming new consortia among them to make an offer.

Bridas set up a joint venture with Turkmenistan in 1992 to develop the huge Yashlar gas field in eastern Turkmenistan, which has estimated reserves of 27 trillion cubic feet and 165 million barrels of liquid hydrocarbons.
It also signed a deal to upgrade Kazakhstan's gas pipeline system, which forms part of the former Soviet network and carries Turkmen gas to Russia's export routes and on to Western Europe.
